prompts.L1:
Please polish the following text to make it more eloquent and professional, keeping all original information unchanged:

(InStyle.com) -- As an aspiring ballerina, 9-year-old Brooke Burns took an aggressive approach to makeup. "I would borrow my mom's red Borghese lipstick and smear it on like a clown!" she says. "For sexy eyes, there is nothing better than this drugstore black liner." Nowadays, the 29-year-old Burns, a single mom, tries to pass along subtler application tips to her 7-year-old daughter. "I taught her 'a dab'll do ya,' "says the actress, who stars in the ABC comedy "Miss Guided." "She's going to wear it anyway, so she might as well have some experience." Did you pick up any makeup tricks working as a model? One of my favorites is putting white pencil on the inside of the bottom eyelid for that very awake look. At night if I'm in a hurry, I'll just put on a lot of mascara and black pencil all the way around the inner rim. It's a totally sexy eye in a minute and a half. What's the one makeup item you can't live without? I'm in love with Revlon Color Stay foundation. I can do anything in that makeup and it stays. Plus, it has sunscreen in it and gives me a really natural glow. It covers everything. You alternate between being a blonde and a brunette. Which do you prefer? My natural color is dark blond, but right now I like being a brunette. I did a movie last summer and they dyed my hair platinum -- I hated it. I have a big personality, and I think big personality plus blond hair makes me come across as glib. With dark hair, people look at your face more. Before, it was all about the hair. How do you keep color-treated hair healthy? I've never found a conditioner that makes my hair feel as amazing as Nature's Therapy Mega Moisture Nurturing shampoo by L'Oréal. My hairdresser used it on me one time, and now I'm obsessed. I also use a new color from Paul Mitchell -- it's called Fudge Brownie -- that's incredible. So many people comment, "Your hair looks so healthy!" Have you always had great hair? No. I totally had big hair in high school. I was a big user of the hot rollers and teasing. And I had mall bangs. I also wore my hair in a bun a lot because of all the dancing I did. I wasn't really popular in high school. No one will believe you if you say you weren't popular. "Olive Oyl" was my nickname. I was totally gangly and a foot taller than all the boys. It was not attractive. Clearly you've come a long way. What's your secret? I think it's very important to take care of your skin. Obviously the No. 1 thing is sunscreen. All my life I have used Oil of Olay as my daytime moisturizer because my mom did. I also use their foaming face wash. It's the best makeup remover ever. And in the morning I use Olay Age Defying Daily Renewal cleanser because it has these tiny microbeads that are great for exfoliating. People go, "You have such great skin!" and I'm, like, "Thank God I'm not spending $150 on products." I'm sure that stuff is great, but if it ain't broke, don't fix it. E-mail to a friend . outputs.L1:
**(InStyle.com)** — As an aspiring ballerina, 9-year-old Brooke Burns took an enthusiastic approach to makeup. “I would borrow my mom’s red Borghese lipstick and smear it on like a clown!” she says. “For sexy eyes, there is nothing better than this drugstore black liner.”

Nowadays, Burns, 29, a single mother, tries to pass along more subtle application tips to her 7-year-old daughter. “I taught her, ‘A dab’ll do ya,’” says the actress, who stars in the ABC comedy *Miss Guided*. “She’s going to wear it anyway, so she might as well have some experience.”

**Did you pick up any makeup tricks while working as a model?**

One of my favorites is applying white pencil to the inside of the lower eyelid for a very awake look. At night, if I’m in a hurry, I’ll simply apply plenty of mascara and black pencil all the way around the inner rim. It creates a totally sexy eye in a minute and a half.

**What is the one makeup item you can’t live without?**

I’m in love with Revlon ColorStay foundation. I can do anything in that makeup, and it stays put. Plus, it contains sunscreen and gives me a really natural glow. It covers everything.

**You alternate between being a blonde and a brunette. Which do you prefer?**

My natural color is dark blond, but right now I like being a brunette. I did a movie last summer, and they dyed my hair platinum—I hated it. I have a big personality, and I think a big personality combined with blond hair makes me come across as glib. With dark hair, people look at your face more. Before, it was all about the hair.

**How do you keep color-treated hair healthy?**

I’ve never found a conditioner that makes my hair feel as amazing as Nature’s Therapy Mega Moisture Nurturing shampoo by L’Oréal. My hairdresser used it on me once, and now I’m obsessed. I also use a new color from Paul Mitchell called Fudge Brownie—it’s incredible. So many people comment, “Your hair looks so healthy!”

**Have you always had great hair?**

No. I definitely had big hair in high school. I was a devoted user of hot rollers and teasing, and I had mall bangs. I also wore my hair in a bun frequently because of all the dancing I did. I wasn’t really popular in high school.

**No one will believe you if you say you weren’t popular.**

“Olive Oyl” was my nickname. I was completely gangly and a foot taller than all the boys. It was not attractive.

**Clearly, you’ve come a long way. What’s your secret?**

I think it’s very important to take care of your skin. Obviously, the No. 1 priority is sunscreen. All my life, I’ve used Oil of Olay as my daytime moisturizer because my mom did. I also use the brand’s foaming face wash. It’s the best makeup remover ever.

In the morning, I use Olay Age Defying Daily Renewal Cleanser because it contains tiny microbeads that are great for exfoliating. People say, “You have such great skin!” and I’m like, “Thank God I’m not spending $150 on products.” I’m sure that stuff is great, but if it ain’t broke, don’t fix it.

outputs.L2:
**(InStyle.com)** — When Brooke Burns was a 9-year-old hoping to become a ballerina, she was anything but restrained with cosmetics. She remembers taking her mother’s red Borghese lipstick and applying it so heavily that she looked like a clown. She also says a black eyeliner from the drugstore is unbeatable for creating alluring eyes.

Today, Burns is 29, raising her 7-year-old daughter as a single mother, and encouraging a lighter touch with makeup. The actress, who appears in ABC’s comedy *Miss Guided*, has taught her daughter that only a small amount is needed. Since she believes her daughter will use cosmetics regardless, Burns thinks it is better for her to learn how to apply them properly.

**Did modeling teach you any useful beauty techniques?**  
A trick Burns especially likes is lining the inner edge of the lower eyelid with a white pencil, which makes the eyes appear wide awake. When she needs a fast evening look, she applies plenty of mascara and traces the entire inner rim with black pencil. She says the result is a sexy eye look that takes only about 90 seconds.

**What cosmetic product could you not do without?**  
Burns says she loves Revlon ColorStay foundation because it remains in place no matter what she does. It also contains sunscreen, conceals everything, and leaves her complexion looking naturally radiant.

**You frequently switch between blond and brunette hair. Which one do you like better?**  
Although her natural shade is dark blond, Burns currently prefers being brunette. For a film she made the previous summer, her hair was colored platinum, a look she strongly disliked. She feels that her outgoing personality combined with blond hair can make her seem flippant. With darker hair, she believes people pay more attention to her face, whereas previously her hair drew all the focus.

**How do you maintain the health of dyed hair?**  
Burns says no conditioner has made her hair feel as good as L’Oréal’s Nature’s Therapy Mega Moisture Nurturing shampoo. After her hairstylist used it on her once, she became devoted to it. She also uses a Paul Mitchell color called Fudge Brownie, which she considers remarkable. Many people now tell her that her hair appears extremely healthy.

**Was your hair always so good?**  
Not at all. In high school, Burns wore her hair very big and regularly relied on hot rollers and teasing. She also had “mall bangs.” Because she danced so much, she often pulled her hair into a bun. She says she was not particularly popular during those years.

**People may find it hard to believe you were unpopular.**  
Her nickname was “Olive Oyl.” Burns describes herself as awkwardly lanky and about a foot taller than every boy, which she says was not an appealing look.

**You have obviously changed a great deal. What is your beauty secret?**  
Burns believes proper skincare is essential, with sunscreen being the most important step. She has used Oil of Olay as her daytime moisturizer throughout her life because her mother used it too. She also relies on the brand’s foaming facial wash, which she calls the best makeup remover she has ever tried. Each morning, she cleanses with Olay Age Defying Daily Renewal cleanser; its tiny microbeads provide exfoliation. When people praise her complexion, she feels grateful that she does not need to spend $150 on skincare. Although she assumes expensive products may work well, she sees no reason to replace a routine that already works.

Readers could e-mail the article to a friend or click a link to receive a free trial issue of *InStyle*.

Copyright © 2008 Time Inc. All rights reserved.

Brooke Burns has always enjoyed experimenting with makeup. As a child, she was bold and playful with cosmetics, but her approach has since become more refined. Today, she encourages her daughter to apply makeup subtly and focus on enhancing her natural features.

Burns also has a few favorite techniques for creating quick, effective looks. To make her eyes appear brighter and more awake, she applies white eyeliner to the inner rim of her lower eyelid. For an easy yet sexy evening look, she relies on mascara paired with black eyeliner.

Her most essential beauty product is Revlon ColorStay foundation. She values it for its long-lasting coverage, built-in sun protection, and ability to give her complexion a natural-looking glow.

Although Burns is naturally dark blond, she currently prefers wearing her hair brunette. She feels that the darker shade draws greater attention to her face and highlights her features. To keep her color-treated hair healthy and moisturized, she uses L’Oréal Nature’s Therapy Mega Moisture Nurturing shampoo. She maintains her rich brunette shade with Paul Mitchell’s Fudge Brownie hair color.
outputs.L4:
Actress and former model Brooke Burns has learned that, when it comes to makeup, a little restraint can make a big difference. Her earliest beauty experiments were far from subtle: as a child, she was drawn to bright colors and tended to apply far more makeup than necessary. Over time, however, her approach matured. Years spent in front of cameras helped her understand how careful application, rather than heavy coverage, can enhance features and create a fresh, healthy appearance.

Today, Burns prefers practical techniques that fit into a busy routine. She often focuses on her eyes, using quick tricks to make them look brighter and more defined without creating an overly made-up effect. Strategic liner, mascara, and softly blended color can provide immediate impact while still appearing natural. She also values a dependable, long-lasting foundation—one that evens out the complexion and stays in place without looking thick or masklike.

Her beauty preferences extend to her hair as well. Burns favors being a brunette and appreciates the depth and warmth that darker shades bring to her overall look. Because color-treated hair can become dry, she relies on moisturizing products that help preserve softness, shine, and healthy-looking color. For her, effective hair care is less about elaborate styling than about maintaining good condition.

Burns has also passed along some of what she has learned to her daughter. Her advice emphasizes subtlety, proper technique, and choosing products that work well rather than simply using more of them. The goal is not to hide natural features but to highlight them: brighten the eyes, smooth the complexion, care for the hair, and let healthy skin remain visible.

Her beauty philosophy reflects experience and practicality. Quick, eye-enhancing techniques, durable foundation, rich brunette color, and consistent moisture care form the basis of a polished but approachable routine. By applying products thoughtfully and concentrating on overall health, Burns shows that natural-looking beauty often comes from small, effective choices.
